messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert 3789012345 - increased OOM rate observed on runtime-pool-us-west-2
alex: seeing container restarts on gpu-37, pods in CrashLoopBackOff. logs show repeated `CUDA out of memory` and `kv_page_alloc failed`
mira: pasting key log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T21:14:02Z runtime[pid=2345]: kv_page_alloc: allocation failed size=32768 slab=kv-paged
2026-03-15T21:14:02Z runtime[pid=2345]: attention_paging: paged-alloc fragment ratio=0.82
2026-03-15T21:14:03Z runtime[pid=2345]: cuda: out of memory when allocating 1.2GB
```
jon: customer telemetry: 5xx spike on /v1/generate, error rate ~1.5% over last 10m, a few support tickets triggered
sriram: initial read: pattern looks like slow memory creep in paged-kv allocator. fragmentation + long-lived KV entries when sequence length spikes above 2048
casey: quick mitigations proposed: reduce max_seq to 1024 via env override, disable attention paging on noisy nodes (`REDWOOD_DISABLE_ATTENTION_PAGING=1`), and temporarily lower eviction threshold to force compaction
alex: taking nodes out of rotation: `kubectl cordon gpu-37 && kubectl drain gpu-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` -> will restart runtime pods to clear kv caches
mira: applying hotfix to runtime config: set `kv_eviction_threshold=0.65` (was 0.85). Patch diff:
```
- default_eviction_threshold = 0.85
+ default_eviction_threshold = 0.65
```
oncall-bot: deploy/runtime-hotfix-3789 started by alex to runtime/us-west-2
jon: rolling update to 3/5 nodes done, OOMs stopped on restarted nodes. gpu-35 still showing noisy OOMs and elevated `kv_frag_ratio`
sriram: connecting to gpu-35, running slab compaction trigger and heap snapshot. Current metric: kv_frag_ratio=0.91, resident_kv_pages=1.2M
casey: recommend routing affected tenants to fallback model variant (quantized-v1) to reduce KV footprint while we stabilize
alex: applied routing override for tenants with >0.5% error to quantized-v1. Traffic shift in progress (~30% moved so far)
mira: customer ops update: contacted top impacted customers, opened tickets, and posted status on status.redwood.ai. No emergency SLA breaches yet but latency blips reported
jon: plan summary: short-term: eviction threshold to 0.65, disable paging on hot nodes, route to fallback; mid-term: offline slab defrag + allocator telemetry improvements; long-term: patch to ensure attention cache free on sequence truncation
sriram: note: reproduced leak in local harness when KV entries are pinned by prefix-cache bug. Created ticket INFR-7421 and assigned self for debugging
alex: handing off to night oncall @casey for observation. Handoff checklist: 1) confirm error rate returns to baseline (<0.2%), 2) check restarts/node <=3 in 1h, 3) escalate if kv_frag_ratio>0.9 persists after compaction
casey: ack, will watch dashboards, running compaction job at 01:00 UTC and will report back. :thumbsup:
mira: impact summary for postmortem: regen API 5xx spike peaked at ~2.2% for ~18m, overall affected request fraction ~0.8% of total requests in us-west-2. Primary cause: allocator fragmentation + slow KV leak triggered by high sequence-length requests
oncall-bot: incident status updated -> mitigated (partial). Channel created: #inc-3789012345
alex: follow-ups: full postmortem with timeline, heap dump analysis, durable fix for paging eviction logic. Owner: sriram + eng-runtime
sriram: will own heap dump analysis and PR. ETA: PR + test harness in 48h
casey: handing complete at 3789015480, leaving watch until 3789019080. If anything regresses, ping oncall immediately
mira: will draft postmortem and include customer timelines and recommended config knobs to expose in Console. :white_check_mark:
